summary: Fase 1 WebSocket pipeline testing complete. All 6 backend tests PASS (6/6, 100%). The new /api/converse-ws streams session → sentence(+binary MP3) → meta → done in the exact protocol specified, and the existing HTTP polling endpoints (/api/converse-fast/start + /poll) keep working as fallback. Echo→Theo rename is correctly wired in both CURATED_VOICES (name='Theo') and KODA_VOICES (keys 'theo' AND 'echo' both → voice_id dJwiFcjz9zW5Pge7G8AG, label 'Theo'). Real ElevenLabs + Claude (via emergent) were hit; full WS roundtrip took ~3.4s (TTFT 905ms, FIRST AUDIO 3246ms, 2 sentences). No mocking.

minor.issue: ffprobe/avprobe is NOT installed in the container, so pydub fails to decode MP3 for waveform extraction. Every sentence frame is emitted with waveform=[] (empty array). Log line: '[waveform] MP3 decode failed: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: ffprobe'. The frontend visualization gets no waveform data, but audio playback and the sentence/meta/done flow are unaffected. Fix: apt-get install -y ffmpeg in the container (ffmpeg ships ffprobe).
Uses deprecated @app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown'); FastAPI recommends lifespan context. Non-blocking warning only.

action_items: Install ffmpeg in the runtime image so pydub can decode MP3 → real waveforms in sentence frames (currently always empty list).
Optional cleanup: migrate FastAPI startup/shutdown to lifespan handlers (deprecation warnings only).
critical_code_review_comments: _converse_ws_handler (server.py:7597) — correct ordering: accept → wait_for(receive_text, 10s) → JSON parse → validate text → create session → send 'session' frame → run _fast_pipeline_task with emit callback → send 'done' → close. Errors send {'type':'error','message':...} and close cleanly. Good.

_emit() (server.py:7646) packs (header + binary) atomically per sentence and sets audio_bytes=len(audio_bytes). Verified header.audio_bytes == len(binary_frame) on all received sentences during the live test.

_fast_pipeline_task (server.py:7078) was refactored cleanly: emit is optional, Mongo persistence still happens via _publish→_fast_session_append even when emit is set, so the HTTP poll fallback keeps full parity.
KODA_VOICES (server.py:4926) — 'theo' and 'echo' both map to the same voice_id and same label 'Theo' as required for backward compat with stored profiles.
CURATED_VOICES (server.py:4520) — male voice dJwiFcjz9zW5Pge7G8AG has name 'Theo' (renamed from Echo).

Note: /api/voice/options exposes BOTH 'theo' and 'echo' as separate options (same voice_id). For the onboarding UI this means the user will see a duplicate 'Theo' card. If that's undesirable for new users, consider filtering the legacy 'echo' alias from the /voice/options response while still accepting it in writes. (Not in scope of this fase 1 review — flagging only.)
seed_data_creation: None. Tests use ephemeral=true so no timeline entries persist. fast_sessions docs are created (auto-TTL by existing index).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_fase1_ws.py -v. Tests target HTTP/WS at localhost:8001 (override via env KODA_TEST_HTTP_BASE / KODA_TEST_WS_BASE). Real LLM/TTS calls — each WS happy-path costs ~3s and a few cents. ffprobe missing is a known minor issue (empty waveform); if main agent installs ffmpeg, no test changes needed because the test asserts only that audio_bytes header matches binary frame length, not the waveform content.
rca_of_issue: N/A — all required behaviors verified end-to-end against real backend services. The empty-waveform observation is a pre-existing container limitation (no ffprobe), not introduced by Fase 1.
